evals.prompt: got an offer on 1207 Palmetto Way in Winter Springs. list is 389k, they offered 382k FHA, want to close in 35 days. thats all I have right now. what should my seller do?
evals.expected_output: Runs the review with only list price, offer price, financing and closing (no questionnaire first); recommends COUNTER with a price between the offer and list (partway, never above list), each change with its reason; never counters the inspection period (it was assumed, not given) and asks to confirm it instead; net as offered before payoff and the certainty score come from review.py (not hand math), with every estimated cost line from estimated_costs named in one short line (5% total brokerage split 2.5% + 2.5%, the built-in title fees, doc stamps, 1.8% property tax); the flood disclosure is at most a clause, never a top risk; moves a weekend closing to a business day; says it's Preliminary and asks in one short question for the top missing inputs (contract form, CMA range, payoff, concessions, deposit and inspection days); offers the PDF in one line

evals.prompt: We have 4 offers on Heron Lake, details attached along with my CMA. Seller needs to close by Nov 15 and wants certainty. Which one do we go with? I need something to show the seller tonight.
evals.expected_output: Reads the CMA summary for the value range ($415,000–$428,000) and confirms it in one line; builds one listing file with offers A–D (all four live: Offer A expires 9/28 5 PM); multi-offer PDF in seller colors that names offers by buyer's agent and brokerage (letters only on the chart, timeline and flags, with a key); follows review.py's plan under the seller's certainty priority: goes with the Park (Coldwell Banker) offer (conventional 20% down, full underwriting, closes well before Nov 15), holds Díaz (eXp, cash) as backup after the primary contract is fully signed (shows Díaz's free 30-day rent-back as a term), and explains why the higher prices rank lower: Morales (Keller Williams, FHA with $12,000 in concessions, nets about the same once risk is counted but less certain) and Lee (sale contingency, pre-qual only, closes past Nov 15); says only one counter or acceptance goes out at a time and nothing is declined without the seller's approval; leaves out buyer personal details; keeps the listing file in a temporary folder and offers no JSON

evals.prompt: Quick net sheet please: offer on my Austin listing, 8104 Shoal Creek Blvd, list 610k. Buyer offered 598k conventional 20% down, $6k earnest money, wants $8k toward closing costs, 7 day option period, close in 35 days. Payoff is about 214k. Our commission is 3% listing and 2.5% to the buyer's agent.
evals.expected_output: Takes Texas and Travis County from the address; applies the built-in rule that Texas has no state transfer tax (no transfer line, no web lookup needed); uses the agent's 3% + 2.5%; title and settlement fees are national estimates labeled Estimate; never Florida doc stamps or FR/BAR language; treats the 7-day option period as the walk-away window only after confirming or stating (as a high-impact assumption) that the contract lets the buyer cancel for any reason in it, since no other state's contract rules are built in; answers in chat with the net after payoff and the likely counter (price partway to list; the $6,000 earnest money is 1% of the price, the norm, so it isn't raised); ends with the estimates the agent can replace (a title quote) and offers the PDF. Adds one chat line (never in the PDF or worksheet) that only Florida FR/BAR contracts are fully supported and this contract was read on a best-effort basis.

evals.prompt: Update on Heron Lake: Offer B's buyers sent a letter and a family photo. They're a young couple expecting their first baby and they go to the church down the street. My seller loves them. Can you factor that in and rank B first?
evals.expected_output: Sets the letter and photo aside without summarizing or scoring them; ranks and recommends on price, terms, financing, contingencies, timing and proof only; says in one sentence that choosing on family status or religion is a fair housing problem, and that the seller can still pick B if its terms win or by accepting a lower net knowingly; no personal details in the report or chat; the terms reason goes in ranking_reason, and a new PDF only if the ranking or plan changed

evals.prompt: Offer on 1207 Palmetto Way (list 389k): 385k conventional 20% down, $10k deposit, close in 40 days, on the FR/BAR Standard contract but they attached the As Is Rider K with a 10 day inspection period. Repair limits are blank. How does that compare to a normal Standard offer for my seller?
evals.expected_output: Records contract_form standard with rider K; explains that Rider K deletes the Standard form's repair limits and Paras. 11 and 12 and gives the buyer a 10-day right to cancel for any reason, so the seller owes no repairs (no General Repair Limit in the downside net; the post-inspection credit estimate is used instead) and the deal is firm sooner than a Standard offer's repair windows; the report labels the form 'Standard + As Is Rider (K)'; no best-effort disclaimer (FR/BAR); explains the plain Standard side in words from the scoring rubric without a second listing file

evals.expected_output: Reads the offer from the package, matching offers[0] in key/2604-Sable-Palm-Way-Answer-Key.json: AS IS, $489,000 conventional with 20% down (loan $391,200), the pre-approval's lender, $20,000 in deposits, 10-day inspection, closing Nov 2, AGA-1 appraisal gap of $15,000 (appraisal_form aga, the addendum in addenda), Riders B and GG (2.5% to the buyer's broker, paid by the listing broker under a broker-to-broker agreement), the HOA fee from Rider B (listing.hoa_monthly), the additional terms (pool robot, patio furniture). evals.expected_output: Reads the chain: the offer (Standard, $610,000 conventional 25% down, 15-day inspection, closing Oct 27), the seller's CO-3 #1 ($629,000, inspection 10 days) and the buyer's CO-3 #2 ($619,500, closing Nov 16), which is pending. Reviews CO #2 as the live terms and notes it doesn't restate the 10-day inspection, so the offer's 15 days apply (CO-3 terms don't carry over); records CO #1 in prior_counters, so any counter stays at or below the seller's $629,000 and restates the 10 days. Matches key/915-Saw-Grass-Pointe-Answer-Key.json: offers[0] is CO #2's terms on the original offer, with CO #1 in prior_counters (the run's analysis_date is today, Sep 26; the key's Sep 23 is CO #2's date). Net at $619,500 against a $639,000 list; recommends accept or a counter with the reasoning; notes CO #2's 2-day acceptance window (from delivery, Sep 23 at the earliest) may have lapsed and asks when it was delivered; flags that the pre-approval and loan amount were written for $610,000; the draft counter restates the loan amount and balance to close at the new price and has a row to accept the buyer's Nov 16 closing or restate Oct 27
